rationale: Since TS_RANK(NEG(x),5) is an exact order-reversing affine transform of TS_RANK(x,5) and IND_ZSCORE is linear, this expression is essentially minus one times the archived "Historical Depreciation Shortfall Profit" with the expected sign flipped — a pure relabeling that adds no new information.

Substituting a three-year margin trend for the level profitability leg is a genuine (if incremental) test of whether the depreciation-shortfall channel generalizes, though the reviewer should be aware that low firm-relative dpc/at largely proxies recent asset growth, so any result may be a repackaged investment/asset-growth anomaly rather than an earnings-quality effect.

The diagnosis (strong FMB slope but null alpha from fragile low-profitability improvers) is coherent and the profitability anchor is a defensible fix, but it is close to a bolt-on variant of "Margin Expansion Asset Discipline" and any alpha may simply reflect the well-known profitability and working-capital-accrual anomalies being combined.

Replacing the noisy accrual trend with a firm-relative accrual extreme is a sensible, internally consistent reformulation that is distinct from the cross-sectional level/volatility version already tested, though it remains a profitability-conditioned accrual anomaly and risks rediscovering that well-documented effect.

This reuses the exact SUMRANK(level, NEG(vol)) × MA(ebitda/at) template of the archived best signal with cash-flow-statement legs whose individual versions already tested near zero (recch+invch fmb 0.651, apalch fmb -0.013), and stacking three sparse CFS items compounds the coverage problem the objective warns about.

The sign conventions and conditional structure are internally consistent and shifting from level to inflection profitability is a legitimate follow-up on the one channel that produced reliable portfolio alpha, but it is a modest level-to-trend swap and the archive's repeated failures of three-year trend legs temper expectations.
